verdict_reason: Both kernels are parity-exact against the released reference code. (a) Contribution: I fetched RobertCsordas/llm_effective_depth analysis/analyze_norms.py and re-implemented its relative_contribution_layer = ||layer.output[0]-layer.inputs[0][0]|| / ||layer.inputs[0][0]||.clamp(min=1e-6), summed over tokens and divided by the token count, using TRUE block input/output forward hooks; BLME's contribution_ratio_per_layer matches it on gpt2 to max relative error 6.5e-8 across all 12 layers ([10.88734627, 0.30756575, ...] vs [10.8873464, 0.30756576, ...]). The two recent fixes are therefore both CORRECT and both required: the reference does form the ratio PER TOKEN before averaging, and it does clamp at 1e-6, not 1e-12. (b) Block Influence: BLME's _block_influence matches icip-cas/ShortGPT shortgpt/metrics.py::block_influence to 7e-9-9e-8 on identity / sign-flip / rotation / random fixtures, with the analytic anchors exact (identity -> 0.000000000, sign flip -> 2.000000000). The last transition uses a forward hook on layers[-1] to recover the block's PRE-final-norm output, so unlike geometry_lipschitz / geometry_collapse this task has no ln_f contamination and loses no layer. (defect_location is CODE because the defects I list live in src/blme/normalization.py and in the summary-statistic design, NOT in the two parity-exact kernels in geometry/effective_depth.py itself.)
comparable_reason: Both headline scalars are depth proxies. (1) effective_depth_90 is a k/L quantile, so its resolution is 1/L: for an IDENTICAL uniform contribution profile it reads 1.0000 at L=6, 0.9167 at L=12/24/36 and 0.9000 at L=30/80 -- a 10% mechanical spread from quantization alone. Across 10 freshly-run models it is at or near the ceiling on 8 of them (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.9167, 0.8333, 0.80, 0.7778, 0.75, 0.25) with rho(n_layers) = -0.810 and rho(d_model) = -0.696. (2) mean_block_influence is dominated by the embedding->block0 transition, which is 0.818 on gpt2 against 0.028-0.204 for every real block and carries 69.1% of the total contribution mass, so the mean is essentially BI_0/L: measured r(n_layers) = -0.695 and r(d_model) = -0.617 (p = 0.057, n = 10). The per-layer profiles themselves are dimensionless and fine; it is the summary scalars that are not comparable.
github_reason: Fetched analysis/analyze_norms.py from the Csordas repo (master) and shortgpt/metrics.py from the official icip-cas ShortGPT repo, then ran independent transcriptions of both formulas on the same tensors. Contribution profile: max rel 6.5e-8 over gpt2's 12 layers, measured with real block-input/block-output hooks rather than hidden_states. Block Influence: max rel 9.1e-8 on random inputs, 0.0 on the sign-flip anchor. One documented divergence with no effect at the shipped protocol: official block_influence maps a zero-norm state to sim = 0.5 (nan_to_num) whereas torch's cosine_similarity eps-clamp gives 0, i.e. BI 0.5 vs 1.0 for an all-zero token; no zero-norm state occurs in any run I made.
paper_reason: Neither source paper tabulates a raw BI or whole-block relative-contribution value for any model small enough to run here -- ShortGPT publishes pruning orders and downstream accuracies for 7B-13B models, and Csordas et al. publish plotted Llama/Qwen profiles with no numeric table. effective_depth_90 is a BLME statistic with no published counterpart at all (task_metadata and the docstring both say so). The verification is therefore code-parity, which is exact.
confounds_reason: Measured over 10 models: effective_depth_90 rho(n_layers) = -0.810, rho(d_model) = -0.696, rho(log n_params) = -0.644; mean_block_influence r(n_layers) = -0.695. The mechanism is not statistical but structural -- the k/L quantile has 1/L resolution (uniform-profile control above) and the profile's mass is concentrated in the embedding transition (69.1% on gpt2). Partial correlations controlling for log(n_params) are -0.249 and -0.074, but n = 10 is underpowered so I rest the finding on the controlled uniform-profile test, not on those.
defects: src/blme/normalization.py DOUBLE-NORMALIZES effective_depth_90. The raw value is ALREADY k90/L in (0,1] (effective_depth.py:87), yet NORMALIZERS maps it to ('n_layers', 'layer count -> fraction of depth') and core.py:484 emits effective_depth_90_scalenorm = (k90/L)/L. On gpt2 that is 0.9167/12 = 0.076389 -- I ran add_normalized to confirm. Because the raw value is near the ceiling on most models, the twin is approximately 1/n_layers: measured across 10 models the RAW value has rho(n_layers) = -0.810 while the '_scalenorm' twin has rho(n_layers) = -0.916 and r(d_model) = -0.607. The normalization intended to remove a size proxy MANUFACTURES a stronger one. Delete the entry.
effective_depth_90 is at or above 0.9 on 5 of 10 models and exactly 1.0 on 4, so it discriminates almost nothing among small models; its cross-model variation is mostly the 1/L quantization step.

The embedding->block0 transition carries 69.1% of gpt2's total contribution mass (10.887 of 15.75) and BI 0.818 against 0.028-0.204 elsewhere, so both the cumulative threshold and mean_block_influence are set by a transition that is not a transformer block at all. A variant computed over blocks only would be far more informative.

contribution_ratio_per_layer is still returned but its docstring bullet was deleted in the current working tree, so the emitted key is now undocumented (effective_depth.py module docstring vs line 96).

frac_low_influence uses a fixed BI < 0.05 threshold that ShortGPT does not define; on gpt2 it is 0.75 because nine of twelve blocks sit at BI 0.028-0.045, i.e. the threshold lands inside the bulk of the distribution rather than in a tail.
